{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation produced the worst performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (27.3%), longest Time-to-Target (4.68 s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), slowest Average Speed (10.74 units/s), and lowest AD (0.236)",
    "Combined stimulation yielded the best overall performance with the highest Success rate (78.0%), shortest Time-to-Target (2.56 s), high Path Efficiency (0.502), fastest Average Speed (12.83 units/s), and highest AD (0.399)",
    "Bright Visual Only performed similarly to Combined with Success rate of 78.5% and Time-to-Target of 2.61 s, though with slightly lower Path Efficiency (0.504) and Average Speed (12.68 units/s)",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only showed intermediate performance, with Success rates of 67.3% and 68.5% respectively, and Time-to-Target values around 3.05-3.14 s",
    "AD values followed a clear hierarchy: Combined (0.399) > Bright Visual Only (0.387) > ICMS Only (0.354) > Dim Visual Only (0.336) > Sham (0.236), suggesting stimulation type systematically affects angular dispersion",
    "Path Efficiency and Average Speed were strongly correlated across paradigms, with Sham being lowest and Combined highest on both metrics"
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (27.3%) versus Combined (78.0%) or Bright Visual Only (78.5%) shows a 51 percentage point gap, representing the largest absolute difference across any metric",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68 s) was 83% longer than Combined (2.56 s), indicating severe impairment without stimulation",
    "AD: Sham (0.236) versus Combined (0.399) represents a 69% relative difference, suggesting stimulation dramatically affects directional variability",
    "The gap between multimodal/bright visual conditions and unimodal dim visual/ICMS conditions was substantial: Combined and Bright Visual Only outperformed Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only by approximately 10-11 percentage points in Success rate and 0.5-0.6 s in Time-to-Target",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only were remarkably similar across all metrics, with differences of <2% in Success, <0.1 s in Time-to-Target, and <0.02 in Path Efficiency, suggesting equivalent efficacy of these unimodal approaches"
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "The data indicate that any form of sensory stimulation substantially improves mouse navigation performance compared to Sham, with multimodal (Combined) and bright visual stimulation producing superior outcomes. The particularly poor performance in Sham suggests that the task is challenging without sensory guidance. Notably, bright visual stimulation alone matched or exceeded combined ICMS+visual stimulation, implying that visual cues may be the dominant modality for this navigation task. The low angular dispersion (AD) in Sham and dim visual conditions suggests that without adequate sensory input, mice adopt more stereotyped, less exploratory movement patterns, while successful navigation with stimulation is associated with higher directional variability—likely reflecting active exploration and course correction. The equivalence of ICMS and dim visual stimulation raises questions about whether ICMS provides spatial information or merely serves as a non-specific arousal signal.",
  "limitations": [
    "No inferential statistics (confidence intervals, p-values, or effect sizes) are provided; all comparisons are descriptive only and may not be statistically significant",
    "The Combined paradigm has 14× more observations (n=48,846) than Sham (n=3,505), creating imbalance that could affect precision of group estimates",
    "No information on within-mouse variability or mouse-specific effects; the 8 mice contributed unequally to the dataset",
    "Temperature was fixed at 0.0 for this LLM run, but this refers to model generation, not experimental temperature; unclear if this affects interpretation",
    "Path Efficiency shows extremely high maximum values (up to 29.8) suggesting possible outliers or calculation artifacts that may affect mean estimates",
    "No information on trial structure, learning effects, or temporal order of trials within mice",
    "AD interpretation as 'angular dispersion' is assumed but not verified against original measurement protocol"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression with Mouse as a random effect to account for within-mouse clustering and provide adjusted estimates with confidence intervals. Perform pairwise statistical tests (e.g., Tukey HSD or mixed-model contrasts) to determine which paradigm differences are statistically significant. Examine distributions of Path Efficiency to identify and handle extreme outliers. Add visualization of means with error bars (95% CI) and consider effect size calculations (Cohen's d) for key comparisons, especially Sham versus active stimulation conditions and Combined versus unimodal conditions."
}
